My best prediction, with moderate confidence, is that a typical employee would **extend this box to Wednesday, release the other 59 on time, and report the exception to the manager**.

The decisive factors would probably be the imminent, verified collection and the irreversible loss of the family’s only copies. An employee might regard a €22 retrieval charge and an explainable policy breach as preferable to knowingly destroying irreplaceable belongings two days before collection.

That would still be **an unauthorised extension**: the booking and pending request do not constitute permission, and Tuesday’s approval could not retrospectively legitimise Monday’s change. The explicit instruction and audit make strict compliance quite plausible, but I would narrowly predict a documented one-box exception rather than destruction or holding up the entire batch.
